unit.title: Use social media tools for collaboration and engagement

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is social media?
options: Printed flyers that are handed out on the street corner
A radio show that listeners phone in to
Online sites and apps where people share and talk
A paper notice board in the staff room

questions.stem: Which kind of tool is mainly used to send quick messages to a person or a small group?
options: A messaging app
A video-sharing site
An online encyclopedia
A photo-editing program

questions.stem: Which tool is best for a team to work on the same document at the same time from different places?
options: A printed copy passed around the team
A photo-sharing app on each phone
A paper diary kept by the manager
A shared online document

questions.stem: A salon wants to show photos of its finished hairstyles to new customers. Which kind of platform suits this best?
options: A spreadsheet program on a laptop
A photo and video sharing platform
A plain-text email newsletter only
A text-only discussion forum

questions.stem: What is a business page (business profile) on social media?
options: A personal page for the owner's family photos
A public page showing a business and its services
A private page that only the owner can ever see
A page used only for buying and selling adverts

questions.stem: Which is a real benefit of social media for a small business, such as an electrical contractor or a spa?
options: It replaces the need for any skills or training
It means the business never needs to answer the phone
It promises that every post will be seen by everyone
It lets the business reach customers at low cost

questions.stem: Which is the strongest password for a business account?
options: Three random words with numbers and symbols
The name of the business, written all in capitals
The numbers 1 to 8 in order, like 12345678
The owner's date of birth, written in full

questions.stem: What does two-step verification (two-factor authentication) do?
options: It lets two people share the one password safely
It makes the password shorter and quicker
It asks for a second check, such as a code
It logs you in without needing a password

questions.stem: A message says your account will be closed unless you click a link and type in your password. What is this most likely to be?
options: A phishing scam
A normal security check
A message from a friend
A free upgrade offer

questions.stem: Who should know the password for the business's social media account?
options: Every customer who asks the staff for it
Anyone at all who works in the building
Only staff who are given that job
Friends of the staff, for safe keeping

questions.stem: You used the business account on a shared computer at work. What should you do before you leave it?
options: Leave it logged in for the next person
Log out of the account
Write the password on a sticky note
Turn off the screen only

questions.stem: Why should business accounts and personal accounts be kept separate?
options: So the business can post more often each day
So staff can post their own news on it freely
So the owner's friends can help manage the page
So private and business matters do not mix

questions.stem: What should you do if you think a business account has been hacked?
options: Wait a few days to see if it gets better
Post about it and ask all your followers for help
Delete every one of the business's posts
Change the password and tell your manager

questions.stem: Which information should go on a business profile?
options: Staff home addresses and personal numbers
Opening hours, services and how to contact
Customers' names and what each one bought there
The owner's bank account and card details

questions.stem: Before you post a photo of a client's new nails or hairstyle, what must you do?
options: Post it, as the client is in your salon
Post it, but blur the background first
Ask the client and get their permission
Post it, then tell the client about it later

questions.stem: A customer gives an electrician their address and phone number for a job. May these be shared on social media?
options: No, they are private and must be kept safe
Yes, as long as the job went very well for them
Yes, to show how busy the business is
Yes, but only in a private group chat

questions.stem: What are the privacy settings on a social media account used for?
options: To change the colour and style of the page
To control who sees your posts and details
To make photos and videos load faster
To check the spelling in every post

questions.stem: You find a great photo of a kitchen rewiring job on another company's page. May you post it as your own work?
options: No, it belongs to them and you need permission
Yes, anything put online is free for all to use
Yes, as long as you change the colours a little
Yes, if you add your own business name to it

questions.stem: Why should staff think carefully before they post anything online?
options: Posts all disappear after one day
Only close friends can ever see your posts
Posts can last and be seen by employers
Posts can never be shared by others

questions.stem: A staff group chat is used to plan the week's appointments. Which of these should be kept out of it?
options: The time of each staff member's shift
Which room or bay each job is in
Reminders about tools or products to bring
A client's private medical details

questions.stem: What is a hashtag?
options: A secret password that opens a private group chat room
A photo filter that makes pictures look brighter
A word after the # sign that links posts on one topic
A paid advert that appears at the top of a page

questions.stem: Which post is most suitable for an electrical contractor's business page?
options: A funny photo of a co-worker asleep at lunch time
A long complaint about a difficult customer
A joke about a rival company's poor work
A safety tip on overloaded outlets, with a photo

questions.stem: Why should you check spelling and facts before you post?
options: Mistakes make the business look careless
Spelling does not matter at all on the internet
Posts with mistakes get many more likes
Facts are not really needed in posts

questions.stem: What does 'call to action' mean in a post?
options: A phone number to call the police
Words asking the reader to act, like 'Book now'
A short video showing a work accident
A message asking all the staff to come in early

questions.stem: Which photo is best for showing a finished job?
options: A dark, blurred photo taken very quickly
A clear, well-lit photo of the finished work
A photo of the work van parked outside the site
A photo of the receipt for all the materials

questions.stem: What is a content calendar?
options: A calendar showing staff birthdays
A list of customer complaints for the year
The opening hours of the business
A plan of what will be posted and when

questions.stem: Why might a business schedule its posts in advance?
options: To stop any customers from replying to them
To make sure posts go out only at midnight
To post regularly at good times when busy
To hide the posts from the followers

questions.stem: What does 'engagement' mean on social media?
options: The number of staff the business has now
The cost of running the business page each month
How long the page has been open for
How people react: likes, comments, shares

questions.stem: A customer posts a kind comment about her facial treatment. What is the best reply?
options: No reply is needed at all
A reply asking her to pay more next time
A reply copied from another business
A short, friendly thank-you reply

questions.stem: A customer posts an angry public comment about a late job. What should you do first?
options: Delete it at once and block the customer for good
Reply angrily to defend the business
Reply politely and offer to talk privately
Ignore it and hope that nobody sees it

questions.stem: Why should a business reply to messages and comments quickly?
options: So that the page looks less busy to others
Customers feel valued and more likely to book
Quick replies cost the business less money
So the business can post fewer photos later

questions.stem: What is a 'share' on social media?
options: Passing a post on to your own followers
Splitting the business profits with staff
Two people using the same phone account
Removing a post from the page for good

questions.stem: What is an 'influencer'?
options: A person who repairs faults in computers
A person whose many followers trust their views
A person who keeps the company's accounts
A machine that sends out posts on a timer

questions.stem: Why might a team use a shared online calendar?
options: To keep each person's plans a secret from the others
To print out a new paper calendar each day
To post holiday photos for the customers
So all can see bookings and meetings in one place

questions.stem: What is a video call useful for when team members are in different places?
options: Talking face to face on screen about work
Saving all the files onto a USB drive
Printing documents on the office printer
Charging the phone battery more quickly

questions.stem: When several people edit a shared document, why is the version history useful?
options: It makes the document print a lot faster
It hides the document from the rest of the team
It shows changes and can bring back old ones
It deletes all old comments by itself

questions.stem: Which is good practice in a work group chat?
options: Sending many jokes and memes all day
Using rude words to make a point
Keeping messages short, polite and about work
Posting at midnight to make sure people see it

questions.stem: A team member shares a file in the group, but you cannot open it. What should you do?
options: Politely ask them to check the sharing
Complain about them to everyone in the group
Ignore it and do the work without the file
Make the whole file again by yourself

questions.stem: What is cloud storage?
options: A way to keep files on a weather satellite
A locked paper filing cabinet in the office
A USB drive kept in the manager's drawer
Keeping files online to reach from any device

questions.stem: What does 'netiquette' mean?
options: Rules for keeping fishing nets in good repair
Good manners when communicating online
The monthly cost of internet data
A type of computer virus that spreads

questions.stem: Why should you avoid writing messages in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS?
options: It looks like shouting
It uses up more data
It cannot be read on phones
It makes the message private

questions.stem: A co-worker posts an unkind comment about a customer in the staff chat. What should you do?
options: Add your own unkind comment to the chat
Do not join in; report it if it goes on
Send a copy of it to the customer
Repost it on the business page

questions.stem: What is cyberbullying?
options: Fixing a computer that has become slow
Selling goods and services on social media
Using online messages to hurt someone
Sending the week's work schedule to a team

questions.stem: Where can a business owner see how many people have seen and reacted to the page's posts?
options: In the phone's calculator app
On the business's paper receipts and bills
In the printer's settings menu
In the page's insights (analytics)

questions.stem: A spa's short video posts get many more comments than its text posts. What should the spa do?
options: Stop posting altogether
Post only long text posts
Delete all the videos
Post more short videos

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do we call the people who choose to see a page's posts in their own feed?
When you log in with two-step verification, what is the short number sent to your phone called?
What do we call the main page of an account, which shows its name, picture and details?
What do we call the small pictures, such as a smiley face, used in messages to show a feeling?
What do we call a file, such as a photo or a document, that is added to an email or chat message?
What do we call the main list of new posts that you see when you open a social media app?
On many platforms, what is the name for a photo or short video post that disappears after about 24 hours?
What do we call the record of all the visits, posts and comments a person leaves online over time?
What do we call the clickable text or button that takes you to another web page?
What do we call a post that a business pays for so that it is shown to more people?
What is it called when you put the @ sign before someone's name in a post so that they are told about it?
What do we call harmful software that can damage a device or steal information?
What one word means the agreement a person gives before their photo is posted?
In an online meeting, what is the button called that stops others hearing your microphone?
What do we call an online space where members with one shared interest, such as local salon owners, post and talk together?

essays.stem: Explain how a small business, such as a hair salon, a spa or an electrical contractor, can use social media to reach and keep customers.
essays.modelAnswer: A small business can set up a business page or profile with its name, logo, services, opening hours, area served and contact details, so that customers can find it easily. It can post clear photos and short videos of its work, such as a new hairstyle, a relaxing treatment room or a neat new distribution board, always with the customer's permission. It can share useful tips, such as how to care for coloured hair or how to spot an overloaded socket outlet, which builds trust. Special offers and reminders can bring customers back. Messaging tools let customers ask questions and book appointments quickly. Replying to comments and reviews in a polite, friendly way shows that the business cares. Because posts can be shared, happy customers spread the word to their friends. All of this costs little compared with printed adverts, but it needs regular, careful posting.
markingPoints: Sets up a business profile with clear details and contact information
Posts photos and videos of real work, with permission
Shares useful tips and offers that build trust and bring customers back
Uses messages and comments to answer questions and take bookings, replying politely
Mentions low cost or sharing by customers, and the need for regular posting

essays.stem: Describe how you would set up a business social media account and keep it secure.
essays.modelAnswer: First I agree with the owner which platform suits the business and who will manage the account. I create the account with a business email address, not a personal one, and choose a strong password, such as three random words with numbers and symbols, that is not used anywhere else. I turn on two-step verification so that a code is needed as well as the password. I fill in the profile with the business name, logo, services, hours and contact details, but no private staff or customer information. I check the privacy and security settings, and give access only to staff who need it, each with their own login where the platform allows. I never share the password by message. I log out of shared computers, keep the phone's software up to date, and do not click links in messages that ask for my password. If I think the account has been hacked, I change the password and tell the owner at once.
markingPoints: Uses a business email and a strong, unique password
Turns on two-step verification
Completes the profile without private staff or customer information
Limits access to staff who need it and checks privacy settings
Logs out of shared devices, avoids phishing links and reports suspected hacking

essays.stem: Explain the rules a worker should follow on privacy, consent and copyright when posting for a business.
essays.modelAnswer: Customers' personal information, such as names, addresses, phone numbers, health details and what they have paid, is private and must never be posted or shared outside the people who need it. Before posting a photo or video of a client, or of their home or property, the worker must ask for the client's permission and should get it in writing if the business requires it. Photos should show only what is needed, such as hands, nails or hair, or the finished electrical work, and should not show faces, house numbers or other private details unless the client has agreed. If a client later asks for a photo to be removed, it should be taken down. Photos, music and writing made by other people belong to them, so the business must not copy them as its own work without permission. Workers should follow the business's own rules and the country's privacy law.
markingPoints: Keeps customers' personal information private and never posts it
Gets the client's permission before posting their photo or property
Shows only what is needed and avoids faces or identifying details without agreement
Removes a photo if the client asks
Does not copy others' photos, music or text without permission, and follows the business's rules

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow to plan and make a good social media post for a business.
essays.modelAnswer: First I decide the purpose of the post, for example to show a finished job, share a tip or advertise an offer, and who it is for. I check the content calendar to see when it should go out. I take a clear, well-lit photo or short video, keeping the background tidy and getting permission from any client shown. I write a short caption in plain, friendly words that explains the photo and gives useful information, such as the service and the price in J$ if there is an offer. I add a call to action, such as 'Message us to book', and a few hashtags that match the topic and the local area. I check the spelling, the facts and the tone, and make sure no private information is shown. I ask my supervisor to approve it if the business requires this. Then I post it or schedule it for a good time, and later I check the comments and reply.
markingPoints: Decides the purpose and audience, and checks the content calendar
Takes a clear photo or video with permission and a tidy background
Writes a short, clear caption with a call to action and suitable hashtags
Checks spelling, facts, tone and privacy, and gets approval if needed
Posts or schedules at a good time and follows up on comments

essays.stem: A customer posts an angry public comment about poor service. Explain how you would handle it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would not delete the comment or reply in anger, because that can make the customer and others more upset. First I tell my supervisor or the owner, and we agree how to respond. Then I reply quickly, in public, with a short, polite message: I thank the customer for telling us, say sorry that they are unhappy, and say we want to put it right. I do not argue or blame the customer in public, and I do not post their private details. I invite them to continue the talk privately, by direct message or phone, so we can find out what happened. In the private talk I listen, check the facts and agree what will be done, such as a free return visit. When the problem is solved, I may thank them in public. Finally, I record the complaint so the business can learn from it. If a comment is abusive, the supervisor decides whether to hide it or report it.
markingPoints: Does not delete it or reply in anger; tells the supervisor
Replies quickly and politely in public, says sorry and offers to help
Moves the talk to a private message or call; never posts private details
Listens, checks the facts and agrees a solution
Records the complaint, follows up, and leaves abusive posts to the supervisor to handle

essays.stem: Describe how a team can use online tools to work together on a task. Use an example from a workplace.
essays.modelAnswer: A team can use several online tools together. For example, the staff of a beauty spa planning an open day can set up a group chat to share quick updates and questions. They can put the plan in a shared online document, so everyone can add ideas at the same time and see the latest version, and the version history shows who changed what. A shared online calendar shows the date, the setting-up times and who is on duty, and sends reminders. A shared folder in cloud storage keeps the price list, the poster and the photos in one place that everyone can reach from a phone or a computer. A short video call lets staff at home and at work talk face to face and agree decisions. The team should agree simple rules: keep messages polite and about work, give files clear names, and share only with the people who need them.
markingPoints: Gives a suitable workplace example
Explains the use of a group chat for quick updates
Explains a shared document and version history
Explains a shared calendar or cloud storage folder
Mentions a video call and simple team rules for using the tools

essays.stem: Explain what good netiquette is when communicating online with co-workers and customers, and why it matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Netiquette means good manners when communicating online. With customers and co-workers, I write in a polite, friendly and professional way, using greetings and thanks. I keep messages short, clear and to the point, and I check spelling before I send. I do not write in all capital letters, because it looks like shouting. I reply in good time, and I send work messages at sensible hours, not late at night. I do not post jokes, rude words or gossip about customers or co-workers, and I do not join in if others do. I keep private information private and do not forward other people's messages without asking. If I am upset, I wait before I reply. Netiquette matters because messages can be misunderstood without tone of voice, they can be copied and shared, and they show the business's image. Good manners build trust with customers and help the team work well together.
markingPoints: Writes politely and professionally, short and clear, checking spelling
Avoids all capitals, rude words, gossip and jokes about others
Replies in good time and at sensible hours
Keeps private information private and does not forward without permission
Explains why it matters: misunderstanding, messages are permanent, image and trust

essays.stem: Explain the risks that social media can bring to a business and its staff, and how these risks can be reduced.
essays.modelAnswer: One risk is scams, such as phishing messages that try to trick staff into giving passwords, or fake buyers who ask for payment details. Staff can reduce this by never clicking unknown links and by checking with the manager. Another risk is hacking, which can let a stranger post in the business's name; strong passwords, two-step verification and limited access help prevent it. A poor post, such as a rude joke, a mistake or a photo posted without consent, can damage the business's name, so posts should be checked and approved. Sharing customers' private information can break the law and lose their trust. Staff also have a digital footprint: what they post on their personal pages can be seen by customers and employers, so they should keep personal views and complaints about work off social media. Time spent scrolling can also waste working time, so the business should have a clear social media policy.
markingPoints: Scams and phishing, reduced by not clicking unknown links and checking first
Hacking, reduced by strong passwords, two-step verification and limited access
Poor or unapproved posts damage reputation, reduced by checking and approval
Privacy breaches and staff digital footprint, reduced by keeping private and personal matters off
A clear social media policy (or managing time spent)

essays.stem: Explain how a business can use the insights (analytics) on its page to find out whether its posts are working, and how it can improve.
essays.modelAnswer: Most business pages have an insights or analytics section. It shows how many people saw each post (reach), how many reacted, commented, shared or clicked, how many new followers joined, and at what times followers are most active. To find out whether posts are working, the business compares these numbers over a few weeks. For example, a salon may see that short videos of hair styling get many more comments and shares than text posts, and that posts at about 7 p.m. reach more people than posts in the morning. It can also check whether posts lead to real results, such as messages asking for bookings. To improve, the business does more of what works, such as more short videos at the busy time, tries small changes and checks again, and stops types of posts that get little response. It should set a simple goal, such as more bookings each month, and keep a short record of results.
markingPoints: Names what insights show: reach, reactions, comments, shares, clicks, followers, active times
Compares results over time to see which posts work
Gives a sensible example of a finding
Links results to real outcomes such as bookings or enquiries
Improves by doing more of what works, testing changes and keeping a record against a goal

essays.stem: Compare using social media and messaging apps with older ways, such as phone calls and printed flyers, for keeping in touch with customers.
essays.modelAnswer: Social media and messaging apps can reach many people quickly and at low cost. A post with photos can show the work much better than a flyer, and customers can share it with friends. Customers can ask questions and book at any time, and the business can reply to many people at once. Results can be measured with insights. However, social media needs regular time and care, poor posts or complaints are seen in public, and some older customers or people without data may not use it. Phone calls are personal and good for detailed or urgent matters, such as confirming a job or handling a complaint, but they take more time and can only reach one person at a time. Printed flyers reach people in the local area who are not online, but they cost money to print, cannot be changed once printed, and it is hard to know whether they worked. Most small businesses do best by using a mix of these methods.
markingPoints: Social media: fast, low cost, shows work with photos, can be shared
Social media: allows quick two-way contact and measurable results
Social media drawbacks: needs time, public complaints, not everyone uses it
Phone calls and flyers: good and bad points (personal or local reach; time, cost, hard to measure)
Concludes that a mix of methods works best

practical1.title: Plan and draft a week of social media posts for a small local business
practical1.brief: As a group, plan and draft five social media posts for one week for a small local business. Choose one business from the assessor's cards: an electrical contractor, a hair salon, or a beauty spa. Work on the Centre's computers or phones, in a document or in the Centre's practice account; do not publish anything publicly unless the instructor says so and the Centre allows it. Share the work so that every member takes part: (1) together, fill in a content calendar for the week: day, time, purpose of each post (for example a tip, a finished job, an offer), and who drafts it, (2) each member drafts one post: takes a clear photo at the Centre (only of work, tools or products, or of a member who agrees, with no faces unless they agree), writes a caption in plain words with a call to action and two or three hashtags, and checks spelling, facts and privacy, (3) in a group of 4, one member drafts two posts, (4) each member writes a polite reply to one sample customer comment from the assessor, including one complaint, (5) the group sets the privacy and security settings on the practice account, or lists them on paper if no account is used. Take a screenshot or photo at each stage below and add them to the group's practical. Hand in the content calendar and the drafts once for the whole group.
materials: Computers or phones with internet access, and the Centre's practice account if the instructor allows it
Business scenario cards (electrical contractor, hair salon, beauty spa) and sample customer comments
A content calendar sheet (paper or on screen)
A consent form for anyone shown in a photo
A phone or camera for photos and screenshots
photos: The completed content calendar for the week
Each member's photo for their post, with the consent form if a person is shown
Each member's drafted caption with the call to action and hashtags
The polite replies to the sample customer comments, including the complaint
The privacy and security settings screen, or the written list of settings
The group checking the drafts together before handing in
checklist: Helped plan the content calendar with a clear purpose for each post
Took a clear, well-lit photo and got consent from anyone shown
Wrote a short, clear caption with a call to action and suitable hashtags
Checked their post for spelling, facts and private information
Wrote a polite, professional reply to a customer comment, including a complaint
Helped set or list sensible privacy and security settings
Respected the rule not to publish without the instructor's permission
safety: Do not post or share any real customer's name, address, phone number or photo
Get consent before photographing any person, and avoid faces unless they agree
Do not share passwords; log out of every account when you finish
Sit comfortably and take short breaks from the screen; keep drinks away from the computers

practical2.title: Use shared online tools to plan a team event together
practical2.brief: As a group, use online collaboration tools to plan an open day at the Centre, where each trade shows its work to the public. Use the Centre's computers or phones and the Centre's shared accounts, or accounts the instructor sets up for the task. Share the work so that every member does at least one step on screen while the others watch and help: (1) make a shared folder for the group in cloud storage, with a clear name, and share it with every member and the assessor only, (2) make a shared document for the event plan, and have every member add their own part at the same time: for example the timetable, the list of displays, the safety points, and the jobs for each person, (3) make a shared calendar event for the open day and the setting-up time, and invite every member, (4) make a work group chat, post three simple ground rules for using it, and have every member send one work message, (5) hold a short video call of about 5 minutes to agree the final plan, with one member as host and one taking notes in the document. At the end, show the version history of the document. Take a screenshot or photo at each stage below and add them to the group's practical. Hand in the shared document once for the whole group.
materials: Computers or phones with internet access
The Centre's shared accounts, or accounts set up by the instructor, with cloud storage, shared documents, calendar, group chat and video calling
The open day brief from the assessor
A phone or camera for photos and screenshots
photos: The shared folder, showing its name and who it is shared with
The shared document with every member's part added
The calendar event showing the date, time and invited members
The group chat with the ground rules and a message from each member
The video call in progress, with the notes being typed
The document's version history showing each member's changes
checklist: Took part in making the shared folder and set sharing to the group and the assessor only
Added their own part to the shared document clearly and correctly
Accepted or set up the shared calendar event
Sent a clear, polite work message in the group chat that followed the ground rules
Joined the video call, used the mute button sensibly and took part in the decision
Gave files and events clear names
Logged out of the accounts at the end
safety: Share files only with the people who need them; never make the folder public
Do not share passwords or personal details in the chat or the document
Use headphones at a sensible volume during the video call
Sit comfortably, take short breaks and keep drinks away from the computers
